Content:
The lore of "Amanda the Adventurer" is complex and involves a lot of theories, but generally, it's understood that Amanda, or rather, Rebecca (the child whose consciousness is trapped in the show), is likely dead in the real world.

Here's a breakdown of the prevailing theories and information:

Rebecca's Body as a Host: Many theories suggest that Rebecca was killed and her consciousness was uploaded into the "Amanda the Adventurer" program by an organization called HaMelN. This is supported by lines where Amanda (as Rebecca) mentions feeling like her body is "rotting," but the feeling is distant, suggesting her physical body is no longer alive but a host for a demon.

The Meat Shop: There's a recurring element of a "meat shop" where Amanda screams that she doesn't want to go in. This has led to theories that Rebecca was murdered there, and the hanging meat could even represent other victims.

Out There Somewhere": In some endings, Amanda states that she is "out there somewhere." This could refer to her consciousness being trapped within the digital world of the tapes, or perhaps haunting the real world.

HaMelN's Involvement: HaMelN is consistently depicted as a sinister organization that performs rituals and uses the show to lure children, potentially trapping their souls within the show. It's heavily implied they are responsible for Rebecca's fate.

While the game has multiple endings and much of the lore is left to interpretation and theory, the idea that the "original" Amanda (Rebecca) is deceased and her spirit is now tied to the show is a very strong and widely accepted theory. There isn't one clear "killer" in the traditional sense, but rather the organization HaMelN is responsible for her demise and subsequent entrapment... so yeah... she's dead. kinda reminds me of Evangelion... also,


In Amanda the Adventurer 2, when Rebecca (as Amanda) and Wooly find the buried clothes, Wooly immediately starts covering them up and says, "You know what else is fun Amanda, burying things." He does this without explicitly stating his intention beforehand.

This action by Wooly, coupled with his calm demeanor in contrast to Amanda's visible fear, hints at his deeper and more sinister role in the game's lore. Theories suggest that Wooly is not as innocent as he appears and may be an antagonist or an agent of Hameln (the company behind the show), whose purpose is to control Amanda/Rebecca and suppress the truth. His quick action to re-bury the clothes and redirect the conversation suggests he wants to keep certain secrets hidden, possibly related to Rebecca's past or what happened to her. The clothes themselves are theorized to belong to Rebecca or her father, Sam, and represent a traumatic event that Wooly wants to keep "buried."

Content:
In the "Amanda the Adventurer" lore tapes, Rebecca says "Bael (Bye yell), Paimon (Pie man), and Balaam (Baa lamb)" as a way to pronounce the names of demons, likely unknowingly, under the direction of someone at Hameln Entertainment. These names, altered slightly for a child's pronunciation, are actually those of powerful demons: Bael, Paimon, and Balam. 
Here's a breakdown: 
Bael (Bye yell):
This is a mispronunciation of Bael, a powerful demon from the Ars Goetia, often depicted as a king or duke of Hell.
Paimon (Pie man):
This is a mispronunciation of Paimon, another powerful demon from the Ars Goetia, also depicted as a king or duke of Hell.
Balaam (Baa lamb):
This is a mispronunciation of Balam (or sometimes written as Baal or even Bael, which can cause confusion), another demon, often associated with wealth and wisdom.
The theory is that Hameln Entertainment was using Rebecca to unknowingly summon these demons, possibly as part of some dark experiment or ritual. The altered pronunciations were likely used to conceal the true nature of the words from Rebecca, and possibly others

Y’know, I just realized something. The entire concept of innocent children ending up in horrific, tragic situations are becoming a more prominent subject in popular video games.
For example, Five Nights at Freddy’s. Children getting murdered, stuffed in animatronic suits, and becoming the villain of the story when all they want is vengeance, redemption, and most importantly — freedom.
A similar concept with Amanda the Adventurer: an innocent child led unknowingly to their tragic fate, and all they want in the end is to be free from their suffering.
It’s interesting how popular this topic becomes, but is still produced in its own special way.

Author: @Captmushy
Content:
Personally I believe this game is more of an escape room rather than straight forward puzzles, like with Poppy's Playtime for example.
Escape rooms are set up where you obtain different pieces of different puzzles at different times 
then you can go back to solve answers for previous puzzles which progressively unlock more until the room is completed
Not all puzzle games are sequential, where you are presented with a puzzle, complete it, then its done and you move on to the next one.

HOWEVER, I honestly think like the puzzle's difficulties were exacerbated by the lack of save states.
I can personally forgive the extreme difficulty of some of the puzzles if failing didn't send you all the way back to the beginning. 
Plus, having save states It would save a lot time and frustration of having to backtrack through all the tapes again.
Hopefully in the 3rd game we get some kind of save mechanic, or AT LEAST an autosave.

At the end of the day, I gotta give major props to Cory,
Even if I disagree with some of his criticisms, they were still completely understandable (i wont lie that flower puzzle was some nasty work lol) 
Brother spent HOURS on this cryptic game to give us some great content (for FREE too!) and I'm super thankful for it and I had a great time watching~🙏
I hope that the 3rd game wont be as ludicrous lol maybe we will finally get some conclusions about the lore (I agree with what cory said about recaps for the lore, its been a minute since Ive looked into the lore in this game and I forgot who some of the characters were lol)

Content:
In Part 2, at the start, they show lights indicating it's a surgery room and a hospital. Later, we see clips of someone young in a hurry as they slowly open a door to reveal an older Amanda attached to wires and still breathing before being caught. In another one of the treasure hunting tapes, Amanda and Wooly find clothes, which, if you remember, are Sam's clothes (public access interview tape). This means that Sam, like Jordan and Joanne, got put into the tapes, and Amanda's body is still alive—so is she.

In the first part, near the colors and plants wall with the papers on the brown board, we see at the bottom that there's a note talking about energy transfer and dynakinesis. If you link it all up with the symbols, it could imply soul transfusion. This leads me to believe that they used ancient magic to trap Rebecca in the tapes, and we were given a hint.

Also, look deeply into the words "I'm *out* there *somewhere*.Notice how she says she's *out* there and not *in* there, but also refers to *somewhere* ? Meaning she may know she's alive and trapped but doesn't know the location. We may be able to free Rebecca in the final part as we're going straight to the main place of operation, where we're told the power of the tapes is stronger, meaning the demons will have more freedom to materialize

Also, in chapter 2, the first 2 takes don't say *Hamelin* but after Wooly arrives, they say Hamelin, giving us a possible hint that Wooly may be a possible AI/Agent for Hamelin which may explain why Amanda/Rebecca said she used to trust Wooly, but not n more and why she hates him so much.

Author: @thegamingwolfe1038
Content: Just finally got around to watching this. I totally agree about the lore. With the first game the story about a little kid being tricked and forced into a game and then trying to find a way out was a really good premise. In theory though, like im sorry once they started adding a cult that goes back centuries to the dawn of time and every single kid is disappearing it just becomes way to much to keep up with. I really wish the developer's stuck with the more simple story of Rebecca getting tricked and forced into the tapes and then she reaches out to kate to help her get out. Thats the story that they should've stuck with. But im sorry theres like a crap ton of horror games out there about a centuries old cult kidnapping kids, or an organization kidnapping kids, its getting boring and worn out. Theres rarely stories out there in games or any media about having to try and get a child out of a vhs tape/animated world. They definitely should've made that the story, theres not really a lot you can do with the vhs tape thing and i feel like adding a huge centuries old cult into it kind of just ruins the appeal of the first game. Like how many sequals can they really have? Its going to get boring just doing the same thing over and over just to find some tiny thread of lore. Amanda The Adventurer is definitely a game that really only need 1 game and maybe like 1 dlc. They couldve just made a dlc that takes you on a quest to try and find Rebecca to get her out of the tapes. That wouldve been a lot better and more enjoyable than having to solve every little miniscule thing just to get like a 5 minute tape of lore.

Author: @lamiyahjackson5686
Content: I think one of the biggest problems with some horror games nowadays is that developers think that complicating the lore / how you get the lore is the same as giving the story depth. In my opinion, Amanda is one of the biggest perpetrators of this. Behind all the complicated puzzles is a story that isn’t even worth doing the puzzles for. Don’t get me wrong, the story is fine but it’s not worth (imo) spending hours upon hours searching and solving puzzles for. Imagine how much better the game could be if instead of focusing on finding the most obscure ways to hide lore, the devs focused on telling a more straightforward narrative that was easier for players to digest. Scrambling around the pieces of a story doesn’t make the story better - it just makes it more annoying to solve.

MaKenna.

Author: @HAZRE.
Content:
I could tell this one burned Cory out, and it was mainly the puzzles. It's not even the difficulty but how convoluted they are. Like tear this piece of paper, burn it until 1/3 is left, put the remaining scrap under the moonlight of the eastward-facing window until the clock chimes 4 times, then spin around in place 133.5 times, bring it around town, double-take four times in a row, eat the scrap of paper, wait 12 hours to poop it out and the puzzle solution is on the paper. LIKE???

Like that level of trifling specificity, but multiply that for each puzzle. It didn't look fun at all. Like sometimes at the end of a game you feel exhausted because it might be emotionally draining but you feel good, like with a sense of accomplishment, but this game is unsatisfying. You never feel like you really "won" because the dev has some gotcha waiting to trip you up, and don't get me started on the lame story. Dev should pick a plot instead of trying all the plots at once then scrambling to tie it all together. 

This game felt exhausting and I wasn't even the one to suffer it. If it wasn't for Cory this would've been a painful experience fr. Poor guy looked like he wanted to sleep for a week after. 😭

Author: @Brianna-lc5qc
Content: What’s crazy is that Cory was inspired to finish the whole game based on Dashie’s playthrough timing, but they both ran into the same problem: the monster Amanda killed them, and they had to start over. Dashie hilariously admitted that if he had to restart, he was going to end the video—and literally, right after he said that, it happened! He immediately did his outro like, "Alright, I’m done" and everything. You can just watch the last 2 minutes of his playthrough for that pure Dashie moment 😂. It’s interesting to see the same situation from two perspectives because I love watching both of them and seeing how they tackle the same problems. Dashie knew his limit and straight up called it quits, while Cory was determined to push through. But honestly, the game’s design was so tough, and I feel bad Cory had to go through all that frustration, searching for an answer that didn’t even exist. I know that feeling—it’s hard to let go when you’re so sure the solution is just around the corner, but in this case, it was like the analogy Cory gave about receiving a car with no key. All things considered, I'm thankful Cory pushed himself as far as he did because when I watched Dashie's playthrough 5 months ago, I just assumed his playthrough was how the game ended. But now I realize that was only half the game so thank you for your patience Cory.

Author: @JovinGhoul23
Content:
I'm an escape room and tabletop game designer, and the puzzles in this game gave me a headache lol.
I've learned (the hard way) let players discover a solution before you give them a question, a lot of frustration can be avoided that way. Give players clear checkpoints, this avoids over-puzzling a puzzle thats already solved and creates an opportunity to introduce new mechanisms. Make impossible puzzles obviously impossible, not possibly impossible. Pacing puzzles is an art, players want to spend 5-6 minutes on a single puzzle at most. About 10-20 puzzles will be in a well thought out game (video game or escape room/board game), and every puzzle flows well and links to the previous one. This was honestly just all over the place. Glad the Shogun played this one so I didn't have to!!!!!!!!

Content:
Cory, this thought came to me the morning after I watched this, and it's been digging in my head ever since. 
The possum has been antagonizing Amanda throughout the entire game, causing mayhem but never causing actual harm. He pounces on her, only to steal something. He's the "Swiper" to her "Dora". And, we found out he can speak, despite his previous interactions with her implying he can't. But the only word he says is Jo. You were saying John, but I think the possum was saying Jo (like from Little Women). That stuck with me. We hadn't had a consistent character starting with Jo in this game yet, but we did have one introduced in the last game. And she was reintroduced in this game officially: JoAnn! And she was looking for her brother, Jordan! He suddenly vanished without a trace while watching Amanda the Adventurer, we found that out from her letter last game. What if the possum IS Jordan?? He finally noticed that you were watching while he was being a menace to Amanda and Wooly, and then he heard JoAnn's voice, so he tried to get to you because he thought you were her! He could've gotten sucked into the TV and turned into a character in order to feed energy into this TV show, since it's ran by a cult. It's already been said by characters in the game that there are references to multiple demonic entities from different religions: Belial, which is the original Hebrew word for the devil, Mara, which was a Buddhist demon who is associated with death desire and rebirth, and Iblis, which is the Muslim leader of the devils. Iblis is literally compared in reputation to Satan and compared in function to Mara, AKA the other demons mentioned in this game!! So, I feel confident in saying Hamln is a demonic cult dedicated to harvesting children through Amanda/Rebecca (who we know was alive for at least part of the process of sticking her into the show bc of the green tape). How and why, we don't know yet.
This game's lore has had a chokehold on me too man, I keep thinking about it. I dunno if this'll help anyone else's theories, this is just what I've theorized so far.

Content:
WILL YOU GO TO HEAVEN OR HELL When You Die? 

Quick Test: Have you lied, stolen, used God's name in vain, or lusted (which Jesus said was adultery, Matthew 5:28)? If so, God sees you as a liar, thief, blasphemer, and adulterer at heart. James 2:10 says, “the person who keeps all of the laws except one is as guilty as a person who has broken all of God’s laws.” 

You will have to face God on Judgment Day. 

If you have done any of those things, God sees you as guilty of breaking His law and the Bible warns that if the guilty die in their sins they will end up in a terrible place called Hell (Matthew 5:30; 1 Corinthians 6:9-10; Revelation 21:8). 

Will YOU be guilty on Judgment Day? 

There's Good News! 

Though we broke God's Law, Jesus paid the fine by dying on the cross so that we wouldn't have to go to hell purchasing the forgiveness of your Sins; granting you eternal life as a free gift. "God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life" (Jn. 3:16). 

Jesus Rose From The Dead! 

He was seen by hundreds of eyewitnesses. He fulfilled all the prophecies of the promised Savior. Defeating death itself  so that eternal life would be guaranteed to those who seek it (1 Corinthians 15).

What You Must Do To Receive Eternal Life Is:

Repent: Confess your sins to God alone and not to a priest. Make a conscious effort to turn from all your sins and turn to God (Luke 13:3,5; 1 Thessalonians 1:9). It is being sorry for sins committed against God and wanting to be forgiven for all your sins against Him (Isaiah 55:6-7, Luke 3:8, Acts 3:19). 

Faith in Christ as Savior: You must place your entire trust completely in the person and the sin bearing atoning work of our savior Jesus Christ's on your behalf alone to save you from the wrath to come and grant you eternal life as a free gift (John 3:16-18; Ephesians 2:8-9). You must abandon the thought that your own personal goodness, your good works or your law keeping will save you from the wrath of God and help you be accepted by God in heaven, do not rely on them, you can't save yourself by doing good works (Isaiah 64:6; Romans 3:10-12, Romans 3:20).

Faith in Christ as Lord: Faith in Christ also means wholeheartedly committing your life to Jesus Christ as the supreme Lord of your life (Matthew 10:35, 38; Luke 14:27; Romans 10:9-13). It means that Jesus takes first priority of your life and you are to be unquestionably loyal to Him for the rest of your life (Luke 9:62), even above: your family even if it means losing your relationship with them, yourself (Matthew 10:34-37, Luke 14:26), your own possessions (Luke 14:33), and yes even if it cost you your very own life (Luke 14:27). Committing your life to Christ also means that you yield completely to His authority unconditionally (Matthew 11:28-30). In doing so, you are acknowledging that Jesus has the right to command, rule, control and govern every area your life as Lord unconditionally. You are giving up all rights to run your life the way you want and you are own by Him as His slave. 

Will You Repent and Believe in Christ?

“For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world, and forfeit his soul?" Mark 8:36 

After you are saved, there are things you must do to help you grow spiritually. You must read the bible and obey what you read, pray to God: It simply means talking to God. Be sure to find a good church to help you grow and be sure to be baptized in obedience to Jesus Christ. Make sure to tell others about the GOOD NEWS!

Author: @WhatLiesBeneath018
Content:
This game is for psychopaths made by psychopaths. These puzzles are purposefully difficult and frustrating and tortuous. I would NEVER play a game like this because I would not enjoy it. I enjoy clever games, strategies, and mysteries, but this game is absolute insanity.

Now for the lore... **SPOILERS AHEAD**

As far as the two monsters go -- the first one is Amanda and the second one is Wooly. Both of them have a good side and a bad side. As we know, Amanda is actually Rebecca who was trapped in the tapes. Apparently, the cult (fronting as a marketing company Hameln) forced Rebecca and other children to repeat demonic chants and incantations to summon demons such as Balaam and Bael. These demonic entities then attached themselves to the souls of the children. This is why Amanda has a good side (Rebecca) and an evil side (demon/entity).

As others have mentioned, Jordan (the younger brother of Joanna) was actually the opossum in the tapes. This is made evident when he leaps at the screen and shouts "JO" after hearing her voice on the walkie talkie.

Sam Colten is the adoptive father of Rebecca. During the tape where Amanda is feeling bad and you must make a story to cheer her up, if you follow Amanda's drawings rather than Wooly, an unnamed narrator starts telling the story... This is Sam's voice. It is speculated that Amanda enjoys the story in part because the Rebecca part of her misses Sam and likes hearing his voice.

It is currently unknown as to who embodies Wooly. There are fan theories of course, but no real evidence... Hopefully this is revealed in a later version of the game.

Content:
In **Amanda the Adventurer 2**, uncovering hidden lore tapes and solving secret puzzles enriches the gameplay experience. Here's a guide to discovering these secrets:

**1. Lore Tapes:**

There are four lore tapes—Orange, Teal, Red, and Green—each revealing crucial backstory elements.

- **Orange Tape:**
  - **How to Obtain:** During the "Let's Practice Patience!" episode, deliberately choose incorrect tools when Amanda prompts you. Persist until Amanda's patience wears thin, leading to the appearance of the Orange tape on the TV stand. 

- **Teal Tape:**
  - **How to Obtain:** After unlocking the library office, retrieve the hammer from the "5 Ways to Hide a Hammer" book. Use it to break the piggy bank, revealing a train track piece. Proceed to the glass case at the library's front, use the hammer to access the Wooly doll and the "Let's Hunt For Treasure!" tape. Play the tape, follow the prompts, and offer the Wooly doll when Amanda requests a toy. This sequence grants access to the office where additional train pieces and the "We Can Fix It!" tape are located. Playing this tape alters the train puzzle; solving it by directing the train through Paris, Mexico City, and London unlocks the Teal tape. 

- **Red Tape:**
  - **How to Obtain:** In the main library, locate the "Silence is Golden in Here" poster with a scannable code. Tear off the barcode and scan it at the library's front desk computer. Click on the "CLICK ME" link, followed by the cryptic symbols, triggering the appearance of the Red tape on the front desk. 

- **Green Tape:**
  - **How to Obtain:** Solve all sides of the activity block puzzle during the "Goodnight!" episode to earn the "A Thorough Routine" achievement. Completing this unlocks the Green tape. 

**2. Cassette Tape and Secret Ending:**

After collecting and viewing all four lore tapes in a single playthrough, a new segment appears in the "Do You Feel Safe?" tape featuring the possum. Completing this unlocks a cassette tape near the library's exit stairs. Playing this cassette in Kate's office reveals the game's secret ending and grants the "Wear Your Seatbelt" achievement. 

**3. Additional Secrets:**

- **Amanda's Responses:**
  - In the demo, Amanda asks, "If you could visit anyone in the world, who would you go see?" Various answers elicit different reactions:
    - "Rebecca," "Amanda," or "You": "Do you really think you could do that?"
    - "Sam": "Wait, that's..."
    - "Wooly": [laughs] "if you can find him."
    - "Kate": "I wish I could still visit her."
    - "Butcher": "No! Why are you being so mean to me!"
    - "Mom": "That sounds like fun."

- **Monster's Presence:**
  - After obtaining the "Let's Plan a Trip" tape, standing in front of the daycare's television reveals ominous breathing sounds, indicating the monster's lurking presence. 

- **Hidden Glitches:**
  - The demo features subtle glitches, including fleeting images of organs, a demonic face, and cryptic messages like "LET ME OUT" and "he tried to find me," adding layers to the game's eerie atmosphere. 

Exploring these secrets offers a deeper understanding of the game's narrative and hidden intricacies.😁👍

Author: @dr4keplaysjr
Content:
Red Tape
How to get it: Usually unlocked by solving the kitchen puzzle correctly using the oven and specific ingredients.

What’s on it: Grainy footage of real-world camera footage—not animated Amanda stuff.

What you see: A person (possibly a researcher or former viewer) walking through the attic and interacting with objects.

Amanda doesn't talk, but there’s static and distorted whispering.

Purpose: Begins hinting at Amanda’s connection to something beyond the tape. You’re being watched.

🟦 Blue Tape
How to get it: Found after typing “Wooly” in a glitched scene.

What’s on it: More found-footage vibes.

You see: The same attic, this time with weird symbols drawn on the wall and red strings connecting items.

There’s a man’s voice, talking about “keeping her contained.”

Amanda says nothing, but it ends with a loud glitch and her face flashing on screen for a frame.

🟩 Green Tape
How to get it: Sometimes triggered after the piano puzzle is solved.

What’s on it: Found footage of a forest, probably the same forest from the "Forest" secret tape.

You hear: Crunching leaves, heavy breathing. A sense that someone is being hunted.

A voice whispers: “She found me... I didn’t think she could.”

Amanda’s voice glitches in at the end, whispering:

“You shouldn’t have watched this.”

🟨 Yellow Tape
How to get it: Solve the safe code or go through the birthday card puzzle.

What’s on it: Someone talking to the camera, likely a researcher.

They’re explaining that Amanda is not just a show, but a conscious entity.

Quotes from the tape:

“We thought we could use the show as a vessel...”
“She’s learning. She’s changing.”

Amanda suddenly breaks in at the end:

“Why are you telling them?”
Then the screen cuts to black.

🟪 Purple Tape
How to get it: Only available in certain versions or after doing a full 100% run.

What’s on it: Very corrupted video—static, symbols, demonic whispers.

There’s a figure (maybe Amanda?) in a cloak, standing in the attic mirror.

Amanda’s voice (but distorted) says:

“He didn’t listen. Will you?”

Possibly the creepiest one—no animation, just dread.

🔎 Bonus Lore Notes
The colored tapes are likely from a secret organization that tried to study Amanda and contain her.

They were probably filming the show’s effects and its viewers.

Amanda is aware of the tapes. She HATES them being found.

Wooly tries to help you by pointing toward the truth, but Amanda always cuts him off.

Author: @ThatLoyalSamurai
Content:
I have a few things to say.  Spoilers: 




"
"



First off, the bad ending being seemingly better than the "true" ending is because in the bad ending, Joanne broke the tape and released that soul, that seemed to be her brothers soul which Amandas monster was only trying to protect, and it's also why Joanne didnt die straight away like in the true ending. So she prevented any chance of helping her brother by breaking that tape, which is obviously bad. It's also why her, realizing her mistake after listening to Kates casette and deciding NOT to break the tapes actually resulted in her death. Woolys monsters whole purpose is to stop the truth from getting out. Secondly, the game admitting that the cult has been around since the middle ages is a HUGE detail because it possibly confirms the Pied Piper of Hameln theory. Hameln or Hamelin is a town in Germany where the Pied Piper nursery story originates from. The pied piper is known for being a piper who rid the town of Hamelin of rats by luring them away with his music and then, when he was not paid for his services, lured away its children. Which could potentially be a metaphor for what the company ‘Hameln’ is doing to kids in Amanda the adventurer. I feel like the fact that this is an actual KIDS nursery rhym make it all the more scarier and highlights how far the devs went with the lore. Thirdly,  Wooly fits the idea of being Sam Colton because we now actually have proof of him being forced to be used to control Amanda and keep her in line. Which is also why she doesnt trust Wooly. Sam said it himself, he doesn't want to lie to his daughter and say she can trust Hameln, but he was forced to anyways. And Amanda has to be aware of this, there is no doubt about it and its why she is so PISSED off when her father is mentioned.

Also, remember how in the first game one of the secret endings was that your soul gets taken and you are placed into the meat shop and store there seemingly among children or just other people in general. What if this is because you are being stored for the demons to feast upon when it comes time to "feed" and the cult of Hameln acts as a way to provide this source of food to the demons or as a vessel and in return they get rich or have a monster willing to do their bidding. OR every time they grab someone, that person becomes a different character in the show. It could explain why different characters such as tables, barns, etc react differently when specfic things such as names are mentioned. Because they actually know those people and understand what is being said but can't respond and all they can do is show their frustration in their emotions. It's why the possum, 'Jordan' recognized Joannes name and tried to respond but couldnt.

Also, if you could get one tape with drawings, whats to say you cant get others using any other drawings? 

Is this theory valid or nah. Cause in the credits when it says REDACTED, what if it is because they have been using the names of Hamlen reps in their actual credits? Apparently the same thing happened in the last game and some people said that the names were hidden until you unlocked another tape and got the secret ending. I searched it up and got this, but don't know how accurate it is: 

In the "Amanda the Adventurer" ARG (Alternate Reality Game), the redacted names in the end credits are "Hunter Bond" and "Hamfan", who are credited as being the creators of the ARG. 
Here's a more detailed breakdown: 
ARG Context: "Amanda the Adventurer" is a popular ARG that revolves around a fictional children's show of the same name.
End Credits: The end credits of the ARG reveal the creators' names, but they are initially redacted.
Redacted Names: The redacted names are "Hunter Bond" and "Hamfan".
True Ending: The true ending of the ARG reveals the creators as Hunter Bond and Hamfan.

Author: @alex-dm3sn
Content: For the train puzzle, it's simple to figure out whether you are missing pieces or not. You just need to notice how many spots *must* have a piece. For instance, the hole at the very beginning when the train heads out has to have a piece. There's also holes by the landmarks that you always need to fill, like the two at the ends of both sides of the London landmark. In total, you need 1 piece for the beginning, 1 piece for Paris, 2 pieces for Mexico, and 2 pieces for London which is 6. You also need 1 more piece need on the left side of London on either corner so the train doesn't meet a dead end. So you need a minimum of 7 pieces to reach the right goal. For the top goal, you can quickly see that you need a piece to go right in front of it, which means you need a total of 8 pieces for it (the 7 required for the train to be able to visit all three landmarks, and the 1 directly in front of the top goal).

Author: @Oogabooga_69
Content:
Alright so I analyzed this when this first came out HARD and under the video Cory watched at the end, I wrote this comment. I found the vid and just copied it.


The monster at the end is NOT Amanda (or the Amanda demon or whatever). That’s wooly. You can see most of its body, and its wool/fungus or whatever it is isn’t just on its eyes. It’s on its body. This is Wooly.

I think that Wooly is supposed to be the real villain (it’s been hinted at and with the glimpse of the monster Wooly at the end it’s kinda obvious), but Joanne mentions the ‘monster’ wanting to protect the tapes. Monster ‘Wooly’ at the very end attacked when Riley took the last one. It makes me think that monster Amanda only protects Amanda, and Wooly protects the tapes because he doesn’t want to be destroyed.

Wooly is probably some form of artificial intelligence that Hamlin created to keep Rebecca from becoming self aware, and it just took the form of the demon that Rebecca summoned, but actualized. Cory theorized this in the first game!

I think I’m fully convinced that there’s definitely something weird with Wooly in the new game and he’s definitely gonna be a problem. The way he showed back up out of nowhere in the middle of the new game is so weird to me, since he kinda died in the first game. I love Wooly, so I didn’t think anything of it. But the developer’s choice of making him the only talking animal, and that animal being a sheep has to mean something. I always thought of this as a psychological horror, and the meaning of sheep in genres like this isn’t lost on me. In the first game, it seemed he was the ‘cattle Amanda was herding’, trying to break free from her control. But in this game I really think he’s just a wolf in sheep’s clothing. Monster Amanda is the only enemy that stayed consistent. And now that I think about it, monster Amanda only attacks when Riley upsets Rebecca. It never shows up unless you do something wrong, but not in the real world, ONLY in Amanda’s tv. What I’m saying is at least monster Amanda isn’t sketchy and we know who it is 😂

In the Toy Ending (if you pick the Wooly plush), monster Amanda tears it up and runs away. Because she’s scared of it! Wooly = Hamlin. I rest my case.

Edit (goin full theorist now, I can’t walk away until I see Cory understand lol): I just think Wooly’s a factor that was used to keep Rebecca’s soul on lockdown in the haunted tapes. And when we saw Amanda in the secret red(?) tape in the recording session (first game), she was summoning a demon (the “man in the headphones”). Wooly most likely took the form of that demon/monster at the end of the true ending. And Cory’s question at the end holds a lot of meaning: If everyone knows the tapes need to be destroyed, why haven’t they been destroyed yet? It’s because of this new monster. This monster is only agitated when the tapes are being messed with. That was NOT Amanda at the end. Amanda only seems to come out when Riley upsets Rebecca in a tape. Never has it once given us a game over for any other reason.

Content:
Alright, now that I've watched the video in full, I almost retract my jokey comment from last time with "CoryXCrashout".

I think Five Nights at Freddy's was the best and worst thing to happen to indie horror games.  Now every single horror game needs to be overly cryptic to hide clear and blatant writing flaws.  The more games you make, the more you start to understand that by not buckling down and writing a story, you are shooting yourself in the foot.  This is one of many reasons why Security Breach was such a disappointment to people.

Amanda clearly means well, but I can already see the cracks with a game series like this.  It continues to happen to a lot of indie horror games like this.  Also, that ending...that true ending was a long monologue.  That...should not happen, that's backloading.

Author: @irs231
Content:
Nice vid but here’s Fnaf lore





William Afton and Henry Emily opened a restaurant around the early 70s, named Fredbear's Family Diner, which quickly evolved into a chain of restaurants known as "Freddy Fazbear's Pizza," started in 1983, under the company of Fazbear Entertainment, Inc. At some point, both of them left the company, with an unknown individual taking over as CEO.

William was secretly a serial killer, using mascot costumes to lure, abduct, and murder kids. His motives aren't known, though widely speculated to be him trying to achieve immortality through researching the paranormal, haunted metal (known as remnant), which he created through the murders.

His first target was Charlotte Emily, the daughter of Henry. She became the Marionette, a ghost who took care of and helped awaken the other lost souls.

In 1983, William's younger son also died in an incident, at the fault of his eldest — Michael. The younger son (name unknown, BV for short) 's fate is still unknown, though often speculated to be connected to either Golden Freddy (an enigmatic spirit taking the form of a yellow bear) or helping Charlie with saving other souls. "I will put you back together" was the last thing said to BV by a debatable party, most commonly believed to be either William, Charlie, or Golden Freddy.

In 1985, William killed 2 kids, and 3 others were later connected to that incident (The Missing Children Incident, or MCI). He was arrested but released due to a lack of evidence. 4 of these kids were Gabriel, Susie, Little Jeremy, and Fritz, going on to haunt Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, and Foxy, respectively, with Susie implied to have been the first to die. The 5th is commonly believed to be named Cassidy, becoming Golden Freddy, though some think it's someone else.

In 1987, William pretended to be a security guard at a new Pizzeria and killed 5 more kids (DCI for short), who went on to be the Toy animatronics. This caused the unimportant Bite of '87.

In 1993, Mike worked a shift at the haunted original Freddy's. Later that year, the location was closed, and the company went bankrupt. He later had some sort of nightmares about it and his brother's death, likely paranormal in nature.

At some point, William went to that original Freddy's to destroy the 4 haunted robots, but ghosts manifested, and fearing for his life, he put on the costume he used to kill them. It was actually a part costume part robot hybrid, though, and due to the leaking roof, the machine snapped on him, killing him. He went on to haunt it and/or his corpse inside.

While Freddy's existed, a Sister Location called "Circus Baby's Pizza World" opened. It was a front for William to kill more kids, with the robots there made to kidnap them. It backfired when his daughter sneaked in to see Baby, and it killed her. She then haunted it. William, distraught, locked her and the other robots from there in an underground warehouse where they were rented out for parties. The other robots also got haunted somehow, likely with melted down remnant from some other kids, most likely MCI. Years later, William sent Mike there to find Elizabeth. Thinking he was William, she tricked him, and the Funtime Robots combined into one amalgam of wires, killed Mike, and used his corpse as a skin suit to escape. He quickly rotted, and they had to escape to the sewers. He repossessed his corpse thanks to remnant, though.

Around 30 years after his death (presumably 2023, though that may be debunked now), William was found by Phone Dude, who stole him and put him into his cheap horror attraction based on the Freddy's urban legends, not knowing William was inside the robot. After a few nights, the building burned down, and William escaped. There's also a good ending in that game where Charlie released the other spirits, but its canonicity is "complicated" according to Scott (FNaF creator).

Mike also had a security logbook at some point, where two ghosts, BV and presumably Cassidy (given it's not him), talked about something.

Finally, after like 50 years, Henry re-emerged and made a fake pizzeria, where he called the Funtime robots, now separated from Elizabeth, herself, and William. He also made a robot that captured Charlie. After a bunch of managers failed to collect all 4 robots, Mike came and succeeded. Henry burned them all and himself, with high temperatures now revealed to work on ghosts, apparently. Fazbear Entertainment, Inc. was supposedly closed for good.

But one ghost, very highly implied to be Golden Freddy, though argued as a random never-before-seen 6th MCI kid by some, wasn't ready to let William go, so he kept him from being released and tortured him in super nightmares.

There's a book series called Fazbear Frights which has debatable canonicity too that'd take place after this, but if canon it's basically just filler that nullifies the Vengeful Spirit nightmares thing.

After all this, Fazbear Entertainment was revived as Fazbear Entertainment, LLC. They kidnapped a guy and gaslighted him into living in a secluded fake house they made for him, where he made FNAF games, in the FNaF universe, as to make it seem like it was all just fake stories.

A VR game was later made, that was a remake of these, but some suspecious circuit boards were sent to be scanned into it, creating a paranormal, digital entity known as Glitchtrap. It appears as a man in Spring Bonnie (William's suit), acts exactly like William, knows stuff only William knows and even claims to be back, with William's catchphrase of sorts being "I always come back". After a bit of shenanigans, it manages to possess a beta tester and makes her his minion. We call her Vanny.

Vanessa, most likely Vanny, then got a desk job at Fazbear Entertainment. Fazbear Funtime Service, a program where animatronics were mass produced and sent for parties, etc. got hijacked by Glitchtrap who made them hostile. He made Vanessa infiltrate the service as a fake FazEnt representative, supposedly fix his infection, but actually just cut off anyone's access to the system other than him, and send a data packet with him to the current Pizzeria — Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex.

In the current book series, most likely canon, there's this AI called Mimic1, which copies stuff. Many think that's actually what Glitchtrap is, just AI copying William. It's an ongoing debate. An Endoskeleton with it installed was sent to the last simulated Freddy's Henry built to burn, where it got out of control, started killing people and in the ongoing story is hunting down a group of teens. As the Pizzaplex was built on top of the simulated Freddy's, the Mimic got control over it too, but was quickly taken down. There's also this boy Gregory who ended up possessed by Glitchtrap and hacking the Pizzaplex for reasons unknown.

Now in Security Breach (possibly 2035), Gregory, out of Glitchtrap's control, had to escape being trapped in the Pizzaplex, as all the robots controlled by Glitchtrap and Vanny wanted to kill him. With the help of Glamrock Freddy, most likely haunted by someone, though it's unknown who, Greg ended up finding a newly built Springtrap in the simulated Freddy's and somehow defeating it. There's also a giant abomination of wires that resambles the Funtime amalgam down there, it took this William away.

This is pretty much where we are now, in gross oversimplification

Author: @bosslevelbros7182
Content:
Toes are the small, digit-like structures located at the front of the human foot. They play a vital role in balance, movement, and support. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the anatomy and function of toes:

### 1. **Anatomy of Toes**

Humans typically have **five toes** on each foot, making a total of **ten toes**. The structure of each toe is similar, though they vary in size and shape:

- **Big Toe (Hallux)**: The largest and most important toe, located on the inner side of the foot. It has two bones (phalanges) and is responsible for providing much of the foot's push-off power when walking or running.
  
- **Other Toes**: The remaining four toes are progressively smaller as you move outward. Each of these toes is made up of three bones (except for the big toe, which has two). These are called the **phalanges**, and they are connected by joints.

    - The second, third, and fourth toes are commonly referred to as the **long toes**, and they help with balance and push-off during movement.
    - The **little toe (pinky toe)** is the smallest and furthest from the big toe. It has three phalanges, like the other toes, and aids in maintaining stability.

- **Toe Joints**: Each toe has joints that allow for bending and flexibility. The main joints in the toes are:
    - **Metatarsophalangeal joints (MTP)**: Connect the toes to the foot.
    - **Interphalangeal joints**: Located between the individual phalanges of each toe.

- **Ligaments and Tendons**: These provide support, flexibility, and allow the toes to move. Tendons in the toes work to bend and straighten the toes, while ligaments help hold the bones in place.

### 2. **Functions of Toes**

- **Balance**: Toes play a crucial role in helping us maintain balance while standing, walking, or running. The **big toe** is especially important, as it bears much of the weight and helps in pushing off the ground when moving.

- **Locomotion**: Toes help propel the body forward during walking or running by acting like levers that push against the ground. They assist in the "push-off" phase of each step, providing forward motion and support.

- **Shock Absorption**: The toes help absorb and distribute the forces exerted on the feet while walking, running, or jumping. They work in conjunction with the arch of the foot to reduce impact and maintain stability.

- **Grip and Dexterity**: The toes also assist in gripping surfaces and can contribute to some dexterity, particularly in activities like climbing or gripping with the feet. The **thumb-like** quality of the big toe in humans is a distinctive feature that supports better walking and running capabilities.

### 3. **Toe Health and Common Issues**

- **Bunions**: A common foot condition where the big toe deviates toward the second toe, often caused by improper footwear or structural issues. This can lead to pain and difficulty walking.

- **Hammer Toe**: A condition where a toe becomes bent at the middle joint, creating a claw-like appearance. It is often caused by wearing tight shoes or muscle imbalances.

- **Ingrown Toenails**: When the edge of a toenail grows into the surrounding skin, causing pain, swelling, and sometimes infection.

- **Fungal Infections (Athlete’s Foot)**: Fungi can infect the toes, particularly in moist, sweaty environments. This can lead to itching, burning, and skin peeling.

- **Corns and Calluses**: Thickened areas of skin that form on the toes due to friction or pressure, often caused by ill-fitting shoes.

- **Toe Fractures**: Toes can be broken or sprained due to trauma, leading to pain, swelling, and difficulty walking.

### 4. **Caring for Your Toes**

To keep your toes healthy:
- Wear well-fitting shoes that provide adequate space for your toes to move.
- Trim toenails properly (straight across) to avoid ingrown toenails.
- Keep your feet clean and dry to prevent fungal infections.
- Stretch and exercise your feet to maintain flexibility and strength.

### 5. **Evolutionary Aspect of Toes**

Toes have evolved in humans for efficient bipedalism (walking on two feet). In many animals, toes are adapted for different functions such as gripping, running, or climbing. In humans, toes have evolved for balance and providing leverage while walking upright. The **big toe** has become more prominent, allowing humans to walk and run more efficiently.

### Conclusion

Toes are essential for our daily movement, balance, and overall foot health. They help propel us forward while walking, running, and standing. Taking care of your toes can prevent common foot problems and improve mobility, contributing to better overall health.

Content:
HEAR ME OUT !
These are the many theories I commented in almost EVERY ATA 2 Gameplays I’ve been.😂


1. Amanda and monster Amanda are related but also separated. 
Like, we knew in the previous game she could transform. But here, it was like there are the same person but with different personalities. While Amanda was in the tv, her monster self was OUTSIDE.
 In the “When you’re feeling bad” Tape, When we have to invent a story (knight, princess, wizard etc..), and that Monster Amanda tried to attack us, Amanda pleaded it to not do this and let us try. When she was happy with the sad story and that Monster Amanda was about to attack us again, Amanda stopped it, convincing it to let us go.
See my point ?


2. The Opposum is Jordan (Joanne’s brother).
In the “Do you feel safe ?” Tape before I think the True Ending, when they all lunched at the screen, stuggling and wrestling to get the opossum away, it screamed : 
“Jo..Jo- JOH !!! Jo-..JOH- JOH-AHH !!”
“Coincidentally”, Joanne’s name is with J.O.A. He was about to complete before the guys shut him up. Why would he randomly start screaming that if he didn’t know Joanne ? There’s no doubt of this.


3. I don’t think Wooly’s on our side. 
Because you can see that Amanda hates him more for some reason, he’s like keeping Amanda from truly “express” herself through the games and…well,
We still don’t know his true identity. If he’s a trapped kid, what’s his real name or anything. In the treasure hunting, when Amanda founded the clothes inside the ground while digging, Wooly didn’t even say anything and immediately looked at Amanda and reburried it, trying to brush it off. Most of all, he didn’t even looked shocked !

And…if you look closely at the True Ending, it wasn’t Amanda who attacked Joanne. The monster was different, had some wool and a more animalistic ferocious head. Especially with that familiar ear raise. It was him. Who killed Joanne.
